title: Regional Traffic Sculptor: latency budget allocator and probabilistic eviction sampler
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We frequently see tail-latency spikes when cross-region failovers route traffic to long-haul clusters. Existing soft-pin and hedging policies either over-shed healthy capacity or flood a single fallback region, causing SLA violations and cost spikes.

Goal: Implement a 'Regional Traffic Sculptor' that enforces per-region latency budgets at the request-allocator layer, applies probabilistic eviction sampling for low-priority flows, and performs traffic fractionation to avoid hard ejections. The feature should: 1) keep user-facing p95/p99 within SLOs, 2) minimize spillover to expensive long-haul capacity, and 3) provide observability and controllable knobs for PMs and SREs.

Scope: This ticket covers design, implementation of allocator logic, integration with the tokenized capacity pool, test harness (integration + chaos), and a staged rollout with telemetry and kill-switches. It does NOT include UI changes in Console (follow-up PM ticket will add controls).
acceptance_criteria: New allocator can cap per-region aggregate tail latency contribution so global p99 improves by >= 10% in synthetic overload tests.
Probabilistic eviction sampler drops <= 5% of requests for 'best-effort' labels under sustained overload while maintaining <1% error-rate increase for 'standard' labels.
No single fallback region receives >30% of overflow traffic during a simulated region outage test.
All important signals (region_latency_budget_utilization, eviction_rate_by_label, overflow_fraction_by_region) are available in Grafana and instrumented in CI asserts.
Feature gated behind a runtime flag and controlled via per-customer config; rollout can be aborted with <5 minutes to full disable.
implementation_plan: Week 1: Design doc and API sketch. Define latency budget model (time-windowed credits) and eviction sampler parameters. Link design doc in links.
Week 2: Implement allocator that maintains per-region 'latency credits' decaying over sliding window and exposes a synchronous decision API used by request director.

Week 3: Add probabilistic eviction sampler that consumes credits when budgets are exhausted and preferentially samples best-effort routes; integrate with tokenized capacity pool to account for reserved throughput.
Week 4: E2E integration, unit tests, and a chaos test suite that simulates region flaps, long-tail device latency, and throttled GPUs.
Week 5: Internal dogfood in us-west region with 10% of production traffic, monitor metrics and iterate on thresholds.
rollout_plan: Flagged behind runtime feature gate 'regional_traffic_sculptor'. Default OFF for all customers.
Stage 1: Enable for internal org + 2 low-risk customers (canaries) at 5% traffic; run 72h soak and validate metrics.
Stage 2: Gradual ramp to 25% for region pairs with historically high failover churn; run 24h windows and check regression alerts.
Stage 3: Global ramp to 100% for affected region pairs with automated rollback on breach of safety thresholds (p95/p99 regressions, error-rate, regional overflow).
Emergency rollback: kill-switch route to completely disable sculptor in <5 mins and fall back to current hedging policy.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Aisha Patel: Initial spike analysis attached; tail cases correlate with simultaneous reclaim events and autoscaler spikes (see links).
2026-02-24 - SRE review (Sora Kim): +1 for probabilistic approach; we should add a per-customer minimum reservation to avoid noisy neighbor eviction.
2026-03-03 - Miguel Hernandez: Prototype allocator implemented; basic credit bookkeeping is working locally. PR opened for early review.

2026-03-08 - Design decision: Use exponential decay window (tunable half-life) for credit replenishment to avoid oscillation during flaps. Trade-off: slower recovery vs. stability. Documented in design doc.

2026-03-12 - QA (Lena Rivera): Added chaos test that kills eu-west-1 and introduces 200ms cross-region latency; observed overflow_fraction_by_region distribution looks acceptable at low load. Need to tighten sampler bias for 'best-effort' label.
risks: Misconfigured budgets could cause excessive shedding of paid customers if per-customer reservations are not enforced.
Probabilistic sampler introduces variance; without sufficient smoothing it could create assignment jitter at upstream services.
Incorrect credit accounting during split-brain scenarios could cause double-counting and unnecessary evictions.
testing_plan: Unit tests for credit accrual/consumption and sampler statistical properties (expected drop rate within 95% CI).
Integration tests that wire allocator into the director with synthetic workload patterns (bursts, slow drains, region outage).
Chaos tests simulating partial GPU throttling, long-tail network latencies, and region-wide autoscaler flaps.
Performance bench: ensure decision API adds <300us median overhead to request director path at 99th percentile.
